## Overview

- Dataset: World Development Indicators (2022) [@worldbank_wdi]
- Indicators used:
  - GDP per capita
  - Life expectancy
  - Inflation rate

## Key EDA Results

- GDP per capita varies widely across countries.
- Life expectancy has a narrower spread and tends to increase with GDP.
- Inflation is right-skewed with a few extreme outliers.

## Visual 1: GDP and Life Expectancy

```{python}
#| label: fig-slide-dev
#| fig-cap: "GDP per capita vs Life expectancy (2022)."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = pd.read_csv("wdi.csv")


plt.figure()
plt.scatter(df["gdp_per_capita"], df["life_expectancy"])
plt.xlabel("GDP per capita")
plt.ylabel("Life expectancy")
plt.title("GDP and Life Expectancy")
plt.show()
```

## Visual 2: Inflation Distribution
```{python}
#| label: fig-slide-infl
#| fig-cap: "Inflation distribution (2022)."
#| echo: false

plt.figure()
plt.hist(df["inflation_rate"].dropna(), bins=30)
plt.xlabel("Inflation rate")
plt.ylabel("Number of countries")
plt.title("Inflation Rate Distribution (2022)")
plt.show()
```

## Conclusion

- GDP per capita and life expectancy show a strong positive relationship.
- Gains in life expectancy are larger at lower income levels and begin to level off among high-income countries.
- Inflation is generally moderate across countries, but a small number experience extreme volatility.
- Overall, the analysis highlights clear links between economic development and health outcomes, alongside substantial global inequality.
